Average of rebrate/feerate is computed as the ratio of the group's average rebrate to its average feerate, rather than the average of row-level ratios.
Average of rebrate/feerate is computed as the ratio of the group's summed rebrate to its summed feerate.
Rows with a zero feerate are excluded, so division by zero doesn't occur. Alternatively, they yield null or an error, or they are treated as missing.
Fee-record count is the count of all joined fee rows in the group, including rows where rebrate or feerate is null.
Fee-record count is the count of only the rows contributing a non-null ratio.
Fee-record count is the count of distinct fee records (feesnode). Alternatively, it is the count of distinct orders.
Groups with a null timespan are included as their own group.
Groups with a null timespan are excluded.
The cross-group average count is the simple mean of the per-group counts over all groups, including groups that are later dropped. This is the intended reading.
The cross-group average count is the total fee records divided by the number of timespan values defined in the enum, including enum values with no fees.
The cross-group average count is computed only over groups with a non-null ratio.
"Strictly above" means count > average, with ties excluded.
The first output value is the average across kept groups of each group's average ratio, with each group weighted equally.
The first output value is the overall average ratio across all fee rows in the kept groups, weighted by rows.
The second output value is the sum of the kept groups' fee-record counts.
The third output value is the average over kept groups of (group count − cross-group average count).
The third output value is the average count of kept groups minus the cross-group average count. This is numerically the same as the previous reading.

The join is an inner join on fees.orderslink = orders.recordvault. Fees whose order is missing are dropped. Duplicate recordvault values in orders could multiply fee rows.

A group whose rows all have a null or zero ratio has a null average ratio. It still counts as a group for the cross-group average and can be kept. It is then ignored by the average of average ratios.
The average of average ratios is taken only over kept groups with a non-null average ratio. This is the standard SQL AVG behavior.
Integer division is applied to the sum of kept counts or the cross-group average, so the average count is truncated. This is excluded by "don't round anything".

The third output value is the average of the kept groups' counts minus the cross-group average count, where the cross-group average is computed over all groups. It is not recomputed over kept groups only.
The third output value uses the absolute difference, which is the same as the plain difference because all kept groups are above the average.
The cross-group average count is a weighted mean (total rows divided by total rows), or is computed over fee rows rather than groups.
